Figure 3.8 Image Description 
Sun rays shine on a plant that can use that solar energy to photosynthesize glucose, 
and in the process creates oxygen and releases heat. Animals eat plants which in turn 
breakdown glucose into carbon dioxide and water, and capture the energy in glucose into 
ATP, (respiration) which cells can use for work like moving, molecular transport and synthesis 
of biomolecules. 
144
TAMBERLY POWELL, MS, RDN
